newsitem.title: USA: BT-MCI deal to get close US regulatory scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: BT-MCI deal to get close US regulatory scrutiny.

text.p: Federal regulators are expected to comb over British Telecommunications Plc's proposed merger with MCI Communications Corp for months, studying just how open the U.K. telecommunications market is to U.S. carriers before issuing a decision.

"I would expect it would take a minmum of six months," said Scott Harris, the former chief of the international bureau at the Federal Communications Commission and now a lawyer with Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher. Said an FCC official who requested anonymity: "You have to closely analyze the competitive opportunities and whether the (U.K.) market is open to U.S. companies."

Lawyers and analysts, as reported, ultimately expect the FCC and the Justice Department will approve the merger. But regulators will look closely at just how open the U.K. market is to U.S. carriers, as well as whether or not the merger of two large companies runs the risk of distorting competition.
Harris said it is likely to take regulators six to nine months to render a decision.
"The (FCC) will carefully scrutinize whether there are de facto market barriers in the U.K.," said Harris. "It has to look at how the market actually operates."

He noted that up until this summer only two carriers were licensed to provide international calling from the U.K. British regulators took action to end that situation, but so far no new companies have been licensed to offer such service.
BT and MCI are geared up for close scrutiny. They expect their deal to close next August.
No. 1 long-distance rival AT&T Corp, meanwhile, has called on regulators to give the deal the "scrutiny it deserves."
A six to nine month approval process would not be unusual in such circumstances. It took that long for the FCC to approve BT's initial 20 percent stake in MCI in June 1994.
